blocks.content: While CVC acts as an apex supervisory and advisory body for administrative vigilance, CBI functions as the premier investigating agency of the Central Government.

rows: Functions under administrative control of DoPT
Does not investigate directly; relies on CBI/CVOs
Has direct investigative powers for economic & criminal offenses

items: CBI is NOT a statutory body; it derives its investigative powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.
CVC was granted statutory status by an Act of Parliament in 2003 following Santhanam Committee recommendations.
Superintendence over CBI's functioning in corruption cases rests with the CVC, whereas administrative control rests with the Ministry of Personnel (DoPT).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) is the apex vigilance institution monitoring all vigilance activity under the Central Government.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is the premier investigative agency of India handling corruption, economic offenses, and major crimes.
CVC is an independent statutory body created under the CVC Act, 2003, whereas CBI is a non-statutory body deriving powers from the DSPE Act, 1946.
CVC exercises superintendence over the CBI's investigations specifically related to offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
Both institutions trace their origins back to the recommendations of the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption.
